title: Microsoft Teams: real-time call queue metrics in the Queues app on mobile
summary: The briefing passes with corrections. Microsoft's notice supports the planned December rollout and no-action default, and Learn supports the licensing and existing controls. The categorical read-only description is not documented; minor corrections should qualify the timing, complete the policy path and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Existing voice applications policies control which real-time reports authorized users can access.
claims.quote: In addition, they also control which real-time and historical reports authorized users have access to.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center route Voice > Voice applications policies > policy reaches the existing policy control area.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Voice applications policies. Select the option to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit. Change the settings you want to allow your authorized users to configure.
claims.fix: Complete the early-stopping route in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table as 'Voice > Voice applications policies > policy > Edit > Real-time call queue metrics', following the Edit a custom voice applications policy steps and Call queues - Reporting table at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/aa-cq-manage-voice-applications-policies.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -RealTimeCallQueueMetricsPermission AuthorizedOnly sets authorized-queue real-time metric access.
claims.quote: [-RealTimeCallQueueMetricsPermission <string>] [[-Identity] <String>]. When set to AuthorizedOnly, users affected by the policy will receive real-time metrics for call queues they are authorized for.

claims.claim: The policy setting is named Real-time call queue metrics.
claims.quote: Real-time call queue metrics | This setting allows authorized users to access real-time call queue metrics.

claims.claim: None is the no-access reporting value.
claims.quote: Reporting values: None - no access to any metrics.
claims.fix: In the row note, replace 'values None, AuthorizedOnly (All no longer supported)' with 'The policy page lists None and AuthorizedOnly; the PowerShell reference uses Disabled rather than None. All is no longer supported.' The differing PowerShell value is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsvoiceapplicationspolicy?view=teams-ps under -RealTimeCallQueueMetricsPermission.

claims.claim: AuthorizedOnly limits the user's metrics to the queues they are authorized for.
claims.quote: When set to AuthorizedOnly, users affected by the policy will receive real-time metrics for call queues they are authorized for.

claims.claim: All is no longer supported for real-time call queue metrics.
claims.quote: The All value for real-time call queue and real-time representative metrics is no longer supported.

claims.claim: Authorized-user access to the real-time call queue metrics setting requires Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Real-time call queue metrics | This setting allows authorized users to access real-time call queue metrics. | RealTimeQueueMetricsPermission | Yes

claims.claim: The policy's described actions require being an authorized user of at least one auto attendant or call queue.
claims.quote: A user must be an authorized user to at least one auto attendant or call queue, and must have a voice applications policy assigned, to perform the actions described in Voice applications policy settings.

claims.claim: The policy's described actions require assignment of a voice applications policy.
claims.quote: A user must be an authorized user to at least one auto attendant or call queue, and must have a voice applications policy assigned, to perform the actions described in Voice applications policy settings.

claims.claim: The global voice applications policy disables all configuration change capabilities.
claims.quote: The global, org-wide default policy disables all configuration change capabilities for all users.

claims.claim: Learn advises not changing the global voice applications policy.
claims.quote: This policy shouldn't be changed. You must create and assign custom policies to allow authorized users to make configuration changes to auto attendants and call queues.

claims.claim: The policy article spells the parameter RealTimeQueueMetricsPermission, whereas the cmdlet reference spells it RealTimeCallQueueMetricsPermission.
claims.quote: [-RealTimeCallQueueMetricsPermission <string>]; the separately read policy table gives: Real-time call queue metrics | ... | RealTimeQueueMetricsPermission | Yes.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center path Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps reaches the documented switch.
claims.quote: Navigate to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for the org-wide Microsoft apps switch used to turn off Queues.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft apps" "org-wide" "PowerShell" Queues'; 'graph teamsAppSettings Microsoft apps allow microsoft apps beta'. Read Update-MgTeamworkTeamAppSetting, beta teamsAppSettings, and beta cmdlet/Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration excerpts; no matching switch.

claims.claim: Turning off the org-wide Microsoft apps switch turns off the Queues app at tenant scope.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. ... Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: Turning off that switch also turns off Microsoft apps such as Insights and Tasks.
claims.quote: However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.claim: The Microsoft apps switch is broader than a control over mobile metrics alone.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes no sign-in or identity change.
claims.quote: The metrics available to users will depend on their role and existing permissions. This feature extends the existing real-time queue metrics experience to Mobile and does not change how call queues are configured or managed.

claims.claim: The metrics are read-only information.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Queues app mobile real-time metrics "read-only"'. Read MC1559637, Manage Queues app and reporting search excerpts. They describe viewing metrics and making participation decisions, but do not expressly establish the categorical read-only restriction.
claims.fix: Remove 'The metrics are read-only information.' Keep the following sentence attributed to Microsoft's notice, which accurately describes users understanding demand and managing availability and queue participation.

claims.claim: The notice describes users making availability and participation decisions rather than an automated action.
claims.quote: Use real-time queue information to better understand call demand and manage their availability and queue participation.
